caveats: **Machine scope, default prefixes, point in time.** Per-user package stores (per-user Homebrew, pip user installs, npm and cargo) are out of scope and deferred to the user-session helper (ADR-3003). Only the two default Homebrew prefixes are probed, so a Homebrew in a custom or symlinked prefix reads as absent or refused rather than installed, and an entry removed during a walk is skipped rather than reported.

**A stalled mount can pin a worker, and the sync waits behind it.** The walk deadline is cooperative: it cannot interrupt a filesystem call blocked on a dead mount, so that dispatch holds one agent worker and later dispatches of the action report `busy`; on Linux it also holds the sequential daily-sync source loop, so every later sync source waits. A persistent SELinux or AppArmor denial on `/var/lib/snapd/snaps` or `/var/lib/flatpak/{app,runtime}` makes `store_packages` constrained, so the daily sync reports a status-only `store_packages` section (the stored snap and flatpak rows are kept, shown as unconfirmed) until the agent's domain is granted read access.

**Linux reports presence and counts, and a per-item failure stays `supported`.** Manager versions and the dpkg, rpm, dnf, pacman and apk facts are not read. A snap with an unmounted, unreadable or hostile `snap.yaml` is still a row with version `-` and kind `unknown`, a `snap disable`d snap is `inactive`, and `.Locale` and `.Debug` flatpak runtimes appear although `flatpak list` hides them; only the system flatpak installation and the default snap roots are read, and the Linux sample comes from a container with neither store, so real rows are proven by a WSL2 capture tree only.

**Homebrew rows overlap `installed_apps` on macOS, and cask and tap rows are unexercised against real data.** Casks install `.app` bundles that `installed_apps` also reports, and its `list_per_user` also lists Homebrew formulae per user, so this is a machine-scope, no-subprocess view of the same store and not a disjoint one. The real-capture host had a populated `Cellar` only, so tap, cask and Intel-prefix paths are covered by synthetic layouts built from Homebrew's own scripts, not by a real capture.

**Windows: what was measured, and what was not.** `docs/samples/windows.txt` is a real `plugin-capture` run of the three actions through the agent's `LocalDispatcher`, taken on a Windows 11 (10.0.26200) host on 2026-11-05 as an NT SERVICE virtual service account (not an administrator, started by the Service Control Manager), the same account class as `NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent`. The three actions answered `OK / FULL`, and the Appx roster keys and the Chocolatey `lib` folder read as that account (119 Appx rows, 118 active and 1 deprovisioned, and 18 Chocolatey packages on the capture host). **`NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent` itself was not used**, so a hardened ACL on those keys or that folder on a fleet host is not excluded (see Privileges). The registry and filesystem code (`RealOps`) compiles only on Windows; its reads, including the refusal of a hard-linked or redirected package file, are exercised there by scratch-tree unit cases. **Windows reports roster and presence, with gaps by design.** Chocolatey's own version is not read: its bootstrap package has no loose nuspec and `bin\choco.exe` is a shim that reports the shim's version (0.12.1 against Chocolatey 2.7.5 on the capture host), so the `chocolatey` manager row's version is `-`. Chocolatey is found only at `C:\ProgramData\chocolatey` (a relocated `ChocolateyInstall` reads as absent). winget is reported as present when the App Installer package is registered for all users, which is not proof that a usable `winget.exe` exists for any user (the per-user alias is outside machine scope). Appx rows cover packages registered for all users only: per-user packages are not enumerated, and a package in the `Deprovisioned` list is emitted with that state and not collected as software. Framework and resource packages (VC runtimes, language packs) are rows like any other. There is no publisher column and no install date. **A refused Windows read costs only that source's section.** An Appx roster key or the Chocolatey `lib` directory that is denied, over the row or byte cap or cannot be listed makes `packages` or `store_packages` `constrained`, and the daily sync reports a constrained answer from either of those two actions as a status-only section for that source: the previously stored roster is kept and shown as unconfirmed, every other source is still sent, and the section's token names the cause. The former skip-the-whole-cycle policy, shared with snap and flatpak and tracked in #6093, is retired.

definitions.description: Reports the packages installed under a package manager, read from directory names with no subprocess. macOS reports Homebrew formulae (Cellar/<formula>/<version>) and casks (Caskroom/<cask>/<version>) over both /opt/homebrew and /usr/local. A formula or cask present under both prefixes yields one row per prefix. Linux is UNSUPPORTED by design: installed_apps owns the Linux package roster, so this action reports `status|packages|unsupported|linux:owned_by_installed_apps` and no package row. Windows reports the Chocolatey packages that have a loose nuspec (lib\<id>\<id>.nuspec), with the nuspec version. Machine scope only: per-user package stores are out of scope, deferred to the user-session helper (ADR-3003). Homebrew casks install .app bundles that installed_apps' macOS `list` also reports via system_profiler, and installed_apps' `list_per_user` lists Homebrew formulae per user, so this action does not claim to be disjoint from either; it adds the manager identity and the cask version.

Reports which package managers are present on the endpoint and their manager-level configuration facts, read from the filesystem with no subprocess. macOS reports each Homebrew prefix found under /opt/homebrew and /usr/local with tap, formula and cask counts. Linux reports which of dpkg, apt, rpm, dnf, pacman, apk, snap and flatpak are present (never a package roster) with apt, snap and flatpak counts as facts. Windows reports Chocolatey (its lib directory is listable, with the directory count as a fact) and winget (the App Installer package in the Appx roster, with its version). Machine scope only: per-user package stores are out of scope, deferred to the user-session helper (ADR-3003). A status row always comes first; a genuinely absent manager produces no manager row, while an unreadable location makes the status row `constrained` with a failure token.

Reports the snaps and flatpak apps and runtimes installed on a Linux endpoint, read from the system stores with no subprocess. Snaps come from /var/lib/snapd/snaps/<name>_<revision>.snap joined to the /snap/<name> mount tree (the `current` link gives the active revision; the mounted revision's meta/snap.yaml gives the version and type). Flatpaks come from /var/lib/flatpak/{app,runtime}/<id>/<arch>/<branch> with the `active` link giving the commit. Flatpak metadata is not read, so a flatpak row has no version. A single snap or flatpak whose metadata cannot be read is still reported, with version `-` and kind `unknown` or state `unknown`, and does not change the status; the status is `constrained` only when the LIST may be incomplete (an unlistable directory, a cap or budget, or a concurrent dispatch). macOS is UNSUPPORTED by design (installed_apps owns the application list) and reports `status|store_packages|unsupported|macos:owned_by_installed_apps`. Windows reports the Appx (Store and inbox) packages registered for all users, one row per HKLM AppxAllUserStore package full name, with its version, architecture and state; the WindowsApps folder is not listed. Machine scope only.

description: Machine-scope package-manager inventory (managers, packages and store_packages); per-user package stores are out of scope, deferred to the user-session helper
how_it_works:
`pkg_inventory` reports which third-party package managers a machine has and what they installed, by reading their directories (and, on Windows, the registry) on disk. No package-manager command is ever run (no `brew`, `dpkg`, `rpm`, `pacman`, `apk`, `snap`, `flatpak`, `choco` or `winget`), so it cannot change anything and cannot be fooled by a broken tool. Every action writes a `status` row first and then data rows.

- `managers` says which managers are present. On Windows it reports Chocolatey (its `C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\lib` directory is listable; the directory count is a fact) and winget (the App Installer package is registered in the Appx roster; its version is the version in the package key name). On macOS it looks at the two Homebrew prefixes (`/opt/homebrew` on Apple silicon, `/usr/local` on Intel) and counts taps, formulae and casks from directory names. On Linux it checks for eight tools (dpkg, apt, rpm, dnf, pacman, apk, snap, flatpak) under `/usr/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/bin` and `/sbin`, and adds the counts it can read without running anything: apt source files, snap files, flatpak apps and runtimes.
- `packages` lists Homebrew formulae and casks on macOS, one row per version directory in `Cellar` and `Caskroom`, and Chocolatey packages on Windows, one row per `lib\<id>` directory that holds a loose `<id>.nuspec` (the version is the nuspec's `<version>`, found by a bounded tag scan; no XML library is linked).
- `store_packages` lists snaps and flatpaks on Linux, and the Appx (Store and inbox) packages on Windows: one row per subkey of `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Appx\AppxAllUserStore\{Applications, InboxApplications, Deprovisioned}`, whose names are the package full names (`Name_Version_Arch_ResourceId_PublisherId`). The version and architecture come from that name; a `Deprovisioned` row carries the state `deprovisioned` and the sync does not collect it. The `WindowsApps` folder is not listed (its ACL denies the agent's service account the listing) and `AppxManifest.xml` is not read, so there is no publisher column. A snap is joined from its `.snap` file, its `/snap/<name>/current` link and one bounded read of `snap.yaml`; a flatpak comes from the `app` and `runtime` trees, with the `active` link giving the commit.
- Linux distro packages (dpkg, rpm and the rest) and the macOS application list are deliberately not here: `installed_apps` owns them.

The final component of every directory path is opened without following a link (parent directories such as `/var/lib` are trusted) and every walk is bounded in names, rows, bytes, entries and time, so a hostile or huge tree degrades to a clearly marked partial answer rather than hanging the agent. An absent manager or store is a complete, empty answer; a location that exists but cannot be read makes the answer `constrained` with a token that names it. Each walk takes an injected root (production passes `/`) so the unit suite runs it over a committed fixture tree.

### What you can decide with it

| Action | Windows | macOS | Linux | Question it answers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `managers` | Are Chocolatey and winget present (Chocolatey's lib directory count; winget's App Installer version)? | Is Homebrew installed, under which prefix, and with how many taps, formulae and casks? | Which of the eight package tools exist, and how many apt sources, snap files, flatpak apps and runtimes? | "Which package ecosystems can software arrive through on this host?" |
| `packages` | Every Chocolatey package that has a loose nuspec, with its nuspec version. | Every Homebrew formula and cask with its version directory. | `unsupported`: `installed_apps` owns distro packages. | "Which Homebrew software is present, at what version?" |
| `store_packages` | Every Appx package registered for all users (Store and inbox apps), with version, architecture and state. | `unsupported`: `installed_apps` owns applications. | Every snap revision and flatpak branch, with active or inactive state. | "Which snaps and flatpaks are installed, and which revision is live?" |

A clean answer proves the listed locations were read as asked; it does not prove nothing else is installed. Software installed outside these directories (a Homebrew in a custom prefix, a Chocolatey outside `C:\ProgramData\chocolatey`, per-user installs, tarballs, language-level packages such as pip or npm) is invisible. Manager versions are never reported on macOS and Linux (they are always `-`; on Windows only winget's version is, from the App Installer package key), because reading one would mean running the tool, and flatpak versions are `-` because a branch is a ref, not a version. For "what is installed on this Linux host overall" use `installed_apps`; use this plugin for the snap and flatpak stores and for knowing which managers exist.

### Diagrams

#### Inside one bounded walk

Constrained means the list itself may be incomplete, and that is the only thing a token is used for. A single snap or flatpak whose own metadata cannot be read still appears, with `-` or `unknown` fields, and does not constrain the action; that choice keeps one odd package from stopping the whole daily inventory.

#### What the daily sync takes

A partial roster would delete stored rows, so a constrained `packages` or `store_packages` answer is sent as a status-only section for that source instead of a short list: the server keeps the source's stored rows, shown as unconfirmed, and no other source is affected.

outputs_note: Pipe-delimited rows written via `write_output()`, two shapes per stream discriminated by field 0: exactly one `status|<action>|<supported\|constrained\|unsupported>|<failure tokens or ->` row first, then zero or more data rows — `manager|<name>|<present\|unavailable>|<version or ->|<root_path or ->|<facts k=v;... or ->|<reason or ->` for `managers`, `package|homebrew|<id>|<version>|<formula\|cask>` for `packages`, and the nine-column `package|<snap\|flatpak>|<id>|<version or ->|<kind>|<revision or ->|<arch or ->|<branch or ->|<active\|inactive\|unknown>` for `store_packages`. A genuinely absent manager, prefix or store is `supported` with zero data rows; an unreadable location is `constrained` with a token, never an empty success. `root_path` is the logical path (`/opt/homebrew`, `/usr/local`, `/etc/apt`, `/var/lib/snapd`, `/var/lib/flatpak`), never an injected test root; a manager row's `version` is always `-` in this release (no `brew --version` or `dpkg --version` is run), while a Homebrew package row's `version` is the real version directory name. A snap row carries the `snap.yaml` `version` (or `-`), the `type` as a closed kind token (`app`, `gadget`, `kernel`, `base`, `snapd`, `os`; `other` for anything else, `unknown` when `snap.yaml` could not be read) and the revision; a flatpak row carries the ref id, kind `app` or `runtime`, the commit as its revision, the architecture and the branch, and always a `-` version (the branch is a ref, not a version, and `metadata` is not read). Linux never reports a manager as `unavailable`: presence is the binary, and a fact whose source could not be read is omitted with its token. A formula or cask present under both Homebrew prefixes yields one `package|` row per prefix; the package row carries no prefix column — the manager rows say which prefixes exist. Every OS-supplied field goes through the shared escaper `yuzu::util::safe_output_field`; directory names that are dot-prefixed, over 255 bytes, or contain a pipe, backslash, control or non-ASCII character are skipped without a token (Homebrew and flatpak never create them), so they never reach a row. This plugin is not in the server's `kKeyValuePlugins` set, so the server does not decode its rows as two-cell `key|rest`; the columns below are the definition's own.

privileges.grant: None expected — the Appx roster keys under `HKLM` are readable by authenticated users, and `C:\ProgramData\chocolatey\lib` is world-readable under Chocolatey's default install
privileges.if_refused: A roster key or the Chocolatey `lib` directory that exists but cannot be opened or listed makes the status row `constrained` with `windows:pkg_inventory:<source>:access_denied`, never an empty `supported`; an absent key (a roster key that does not exist reads as no rows) or an absent Chocolatey is zero rows and `supported`
privileges.measured: Measured on a Windows 11 build host, 2026-11-05, as a non-admin NT SERVICE virtual service account (the same account class as `NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent`; `docs/samples/windows.txt` is that capture, see caveat 5), and the mechanisms were also hand-captured as the interactive administrator on 2026-11-04. **`NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent` itself was not used,** so a hardened ACL on the Appx roster keys or the Chocolatey `lib` tree on a fleet host is not excluded, and the package folders under `C:\Program Files\WindowsApps` (which this plugin does not list) are known to deny some accounts
privileges.runs_as: agent service account (LocalSystem today, #1442; `NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent` in the packaged install)

privileges.grant: None documented — Homebrew's `Cellar`, `Caskroom` and `Library/Taps` are ordinary directories
privileges.if_refused: A location that exists but cannot be opened or listed makes the status row `constrained` with `macos:<source>:permission_denied` (or another detail token); a missing prefix is zero rows and `supported`, never a failure
privileges.measured: Measured unprivileged (euid 501) on an Apple-silicon Mac, 2026-10-14 (`docs/samples/macos.txt`; the walk tests use a real formulae-only capture, `tests/unit/fixtures/wave10/pkg_inventory/macos/provenance.txt`); not yet measured under the root LaunchDaemon identity
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, root today (LaunchDaemon carries no `UserName` key — `docs/agent-privilege-model.md` TL;DR); this plugin's own reads need no elevation beyond that default

privileges.grant: None documented — `/usr/bin`, `/etc/apt/sources.list.d`, `/var/lib/snapd/snaps`, `/snap/<name>/current` and `/var/lib/flatpak/{app,runtime}` are expected to be world-readable under snapd's and flatpak's default install modes (0755), as are snap's squashfs mounts (inferred, not measured); not measured as the unprivileged user on a live snapd or flatpak host
privileges.if_refused: A directory that exists but cannot be opened or listed makes `store_packages` `constrained` with `linux:<source>:permission_denied`; a snap or flatpak whose own metadata cannot be read (an unreadable `snap.yaml`, a mount the agent cannot enter) is still reported, with version `-` and kind or state `unknown`, and the status stays `supported` (caveat 3). `packages` reports `status|packages|unsupported|linux:owned_by_installed_apps`
privileges.measured: Measured as euid 0 AND as uid 1000 in a Debian container, 2026-10-14 (`docs/samples/linux.txt`; that container has neither snapd nor flatpak, so the real snap and flatpak rows are proven by the committed capture tree from a WSL2 Ubuntu 26.04.1 host, `tests/unit/fixtures/wave10/pkg_inventory/linux/provenance.txt`). An unprivileged read of a squashfuse-mounted `/snap/<name>/<rev>` under LXD is UNMEASURED
privileges.runs_as: agent daemon, default (the packaged unit runs as the unprivileged `yuzu-agent` user, `docs/agent-privilege-model.md`)

result_status.when: The read completed: managers, packages or store packages were found, or none were (an absent manager, prefix or store is a complete answer, not a degradation). A per-item degradation (below) is also `OK`.

At least one location could not be read completely, so the LIST may be incomplete. `<os>` is `macos`, `linux` or `windows`; `<source>` names the location (Windows tokens read `windows:pkg_inventory:<source>:<cause>` with `<source>` one of `appx_applications`, `appx_inbox`, `appx_deprovisioned`, `chocolatey_lib` and `<cause>` one of `access_denied`, `open_failed`, `entry_cap` (4,096 roster keys or 2,048 Chocolatey directories), `enum_failed`, `row_cap` or `byte_cap`; `homebrew_taps`, `homebrew_cellar`, `homebrew_caskroom`; Linux `tool_dir`, `<tool>_bin`, `apt_sources_d`, `snapd_snaps`, `flatpak_app`, `flatpak_runtime`, and `store_packages` for the row caps); `<detail>` is `permission_denied`, `not_a_directory` (also what a symlink reads as: the kernel answers ENOTDIR to a no-follow directory open of a link), `symlink_refused` (a symlink loop in the path), `io_error`, `entry_cap` (4,096 names per directory) or `enumeration_error` (directory listing truncated or errored: its count fact is omitted, never reported as a lower bound), `row_cap` (20,000 rows), `byte_cap` (1 MiB of rows) or `walk_budget` (200,000 entries or 10 s per action; the locations not yet read are skipped and the rows already found are kept). The wall clock is cooperative: it is checked per directory and per listed entry and cannot interrupt a filesystem call that blocks on a stalled mount inside the tree (a very large listing of non-directory entries can overshoot it by the cost of its stat calls), so `<os>:<source>:busy` (source is the action name) means another dispatch of this action is still walking: nothing was read, there are no rows, retry later (at most one walk per action runs at a time). A symlinked Homebrew prefix, marker directory or store directory is refused, never followed. Several tokens are comma-joined.

**Per-item degradation is not a constraint.** On Linux `store_packages`, a single snap or flatpak whose own fields cannot be read is still emitted: an unreadable, oversized, symlinked or non-regular `snap.yaml`, a missing or unmounted revision, a `version:` that is not a plain one-line scalar passing snapd's version grammar, a broken `current` or `active` link, or an absent or unopenable `/snap` mount directory give version `-`, kind `unknown` or state `unknown` or `inactive` on the data row, and no token. The status stays `supported` because the list is complete, and the installed-software collector fails any constrained `store_packages` answer (a partial roster would delete stored rows), so a persistent per-item anomaly must never constrain the action. `linux:*` tokens therefore mean list incompleteness only. The same rule holds on Windows: a Chocolatey `nuspec` that is missing a version, unreadable, a reparse point or oversized gives a row with version `-`, and an Appx key whose name does not parse as a package full name gives a row with version and arch `-`, in both cases with no token; a Chocolatey directory with no loose nuspec is not a package row at all. `windows:*` tokens mean list incompleteness only.
Linux `packages`: unsupported by design; `installed_apps.list_inventory` owns the Linux package roster.
macOS `store_packages`: unsupported by design; `installed_apps` owns the macOS application list.

Retired: no leg emits it now that the Windows legs ship. The constant stays in `pkg_inventory_parsers.hpp` only because the token-grammar tests still pin it; a host or tool that still sees it is running an older agent.

Any action, any OS: a leg threw during a read. `execute()` catches it, writes `status|<action>|constrained|pkg_inventory:exception` (the one row whose level is `constrained` while the typed status is UNAVAILABLE: the command failed, rc 1) with this fixed token, never the exception's own text, and never lets the exception cross the plugin ABI.

stamp.privilege: NT SERVICE virtual service account (not an administrator; NT SERVICE\YuzuAgent itself not used)

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result AND daily-sync inventory.** Rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore, queryable at `/api/responses/{id}`. The three actions are gathered definitions (`crossplatform.software.package_managers`, `crossplatform.software.package_manager_packages` and `crossplatform.software.store_packages`, 300s TTL).

**Also consumed by** the `installed_software` daily-sync source (`agents/core/src/sync_source_installed_software.cpp`), which calls all three actions in-process on the agent's 24 h schedule: `packages` rows become `pkg` (formula) / `app` (cask) rows with ecosystem `brew`; `managers` becomes one `homebrew` presence row, and `chocolatey` and `winget` presence rows on Windows (every other manager name, including the Linux ones, is read but not mapped); Windows `packages` rows map to ecosystem `chocolatey`, kind `pkg`, and Windows `store_packages` rows (ACTIVE only) to ecosystem `appx`, kind `app`, named by the package name with the version and arch from the row (`deprovisioned` rows are not collected); `store_packages` maps ACTIVE rows only, to ecosystem `snap` (kind `app` when the snap type is app, else `pkg`; version from `snap.yaml`; release = the revision) and ecosystem `flatpak` (kind `app` for apps, `pkg` for runtimes; version EMPTY because the branch is a ref and not a version; release = the commit; arch). An inactive or unknown revision is on the wire but is not installed software and never reaches the catalogue. A constrained answer from any of the three actions (`managers`, `packages` or `store_packages`) is a status-only section for that source and contributes no rows, not even the manager rows it did see: the server keeps that source's stored rows, shown as unconfirmed, and no other source is affected. Not consumed by Echo, DEX, or metrics.

**Sensitivity.** Rows name installed software (Homebrew formula and cask names and versions, snap and flatpak ids, versions, revisions and commits) and the package managers and Homebrew prefixes present on the host with their counts — a software inventory by another route. No row carries a username, account name or user-profile path.

**Siblings:** `installed_apps` (owns the Linux distro-package roster and the macOS application list, and its `list_per_user` also lists Homebrew formulae per user — see caveat 4 for both overlaps) and `software_actions` (installs and removes software; this plugin only reads).
